problems.why: Shannon's zero-error capacity of the 7-cycle is one of the oldest open problems in information theory (Shannon 1956; Lovász settled the 5-cycle in 1979). The best known independent set in the fifth power has 367 vertices (Polak and Schrijver 2018), and one of 368 would by itself beat every recursive bound on Tao's page.

problems.statement: Find as large an independent set as possible in C_7^5, the fifth strong power of the 7-cycle (two distinct 5-tuples over Z_7 are adjacent when every coordinate is equal or differs by 1 mod 7). An independent set of size a gives the Shannon capacity bound Theta(C_7) >= a^(1/5). The largest known has 367 vertices (Polak and Schrijver, 2018); a larger one improves it. Tao's page 9a lists better capacity bounds from much higher powers.
